name: Plan and allocate self-perform crews
summary: Each week the general foremen in a region collect labour requests from superintendents, check them against project schedules, the trades on payroll, training records and formwork availability, and draft a crew board. The director of self-perform operations settles conflicts between projects at a weekly call with operations managers and decides whether to call extra trades from the union hall or lay some off. Weather, failed inspections and late subcontractors move pours daily, so the plan is redone through the week, and the spreadsheet board and phone calls make it easy for crews to sit idle or turn up at the wrong site.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 people with about 1,330 union trades in concrete, formwork, carpentry and labour crews, planned by region.
baseline.notes: Plans are made per region or sub-region (Greater Toronto, Ottawa, southwestern Ontario, Western, Atlantic), about four plans a week.

trigger: The weekly planning cycle starts when superintendents send their labour requests for the coming weeks.
end_state: The crew plan has been approved and published, hires and layoffs requested, the week has been worked with daily changes, and planned and actual crew hours have been reconciled.

volume.seasonality: Plans are made every week; hiring requests peak in April and May and layoffs in November to January.

evidence.note: Org file estimate: about four regional plans a week.
Time all superintendents spend on weekly labour requests; estimate.
About 4 general foremen planning crews in each region part-time; estimate.
Two directors in the org file; estimate.
Weekly crew call attendance; operations-manager is not listed in the process map roles.
Equipment and formwork check for the plan; not listed in the process map roles.

systems.name: Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)
Field time capture (paper sheets or tablet app keyed to cost codes)
Safety management system (hazard assessments, inspections, incidents, training records)
Equipment management (fleet register, rates, maintenance work orders)

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Superintendents submit next week's labour requests
steps.description: Each superintendent in the region fills in the self-perform labour request sheet for the coming two weeks: crews, trades and headcount by day, pours planned and any special tickets needed. Touch time is the total for all superintendents feeding one regional plan, about 20 to 35 projects.

error.defect_description: Request understates or overstates crew needs, or omits a pour.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Pull lookahead schedules for projects in the region
steps.description: The general foreman opens each project's three-week lookahead and master schedule extract and lists the concrete and carpentry activities that need self-perform crews, so he can test the superintendents' requests against the schedule.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Compile requests on the regional crew board
steps.description: The general foreman types every request into the regional crew board spreadsheet, one row per crew per day, and totals demand by trade (carpenters, finishers, labourers, operators) against the crews now on payroll.

error.defect_description: Request keyed to the wrong day or project.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Check who is available next week
steps.description: The general foreman checks the timekeeping and HR records for the current crew roster, vacations, injured workers on modified duties, apprentices due at school and anyone on layoff who can be recalled.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Check training and tickets for assigned work
steps.description: The general foreman checks in the safety system that the workers he plans to send hold the training the work needs, such as working at heights, fall arrest, rigging or powder-actuated tools, and flags who must attend training before starting.

error.defect_description: Worker assigned without a current ticket.

control.basis: Ontario O. Reg. 297/13 working-at-heights training and O. Reg. 213/91 competent-worker requirements; equivalent rules in other provinces

evidence.note: Training rule named from general knowledge; not opened.

steps.name: Confirm formwork and equipment for the planned pours
steps.description: The yard coordinator checks the equipment register for the formwork sets, shoring, telehandlers and tower crane time the crews will need and tells the general foreman which pours lack forms or machines.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Draft the crew allocation
steps.description: The general foreman matches foremen and crews to projects for each day, keeps experienced foremen on the hardest pours, splits crews where two pours overlap and lists the shortfall or surplus by trade.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Hold the weekly crew planning meeting
steps.description: The director of self-perform operations chairs the weekly call with the region's general foremen and operations managers, walks the draft plan project by project and hears which pours the projects say cannot move.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Operations managers press project priorities
steps.description: Operations managers for the projects argue for their pours and schedule milestones, offer to move work to free a crew and commit their superintendents to dates the crews can meet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Resolve conflicts and set pour priorities
steps.description: The director decides which pours get crews when demand exceeds supply, based on contract milestones, liquidated damages exposure and crane and formwork availability, and decides whether to hire, lay off or hold the workforce level.

evidence.note: Branch shares are estimates averaged over the year; spring is mostly hiring and late fall mostly layoffs.

steps.name: Call the union hall for trades
steps.description: The general foreman phones the union business agent or dispatcher with the number of carpenters, labourers or finishers needed, the start date and site, and names any members the company wants by name request, then sends the hire request to HR.

control.basis: ICI collective agreements: trades hired through the union dispatch and name-request rules

evidence.note: Union hiring practice from general knowledge of Ontario ICI agreements; agreement text not opened.

steps.name: Union dispatches trades
steps.description: The union hall sends members from its out-of-work list with dispatch slips. In busy months the hall may not fill the request fully or on time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Cover the shortfall
steps.description: The director borrows a crew from a neighbouring region, adds overtime or a Saturday shift, or asks the project to move a pour, and updates the plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Issue layoff notices
steps.description: The general foreman chooses which trades to lay off, tells their foremen and the union, and sends the layoff notice to HR and payroll for the record of employment and final pay.

evidence.note: Construction employees in Ontario are generally exempt from statutory termination notice under the Employment Standards Act regulations; layoffs follow the collective agreement. From general knowledge, not opened.

steps.name: Approve the weekly crew plan
steps.description: The director reviews the final crew board, checks overtime and total crew cost against the week before and approves it for release to the projects.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Send crew assignments to foremen and superintendents
steps.description: The general foreman emails the crew board and phones or texts each foreman with his project, start time, pour dates and crew members, and tells superintendents which crews they get.

error.defect_description: Foreman given the wrong site or date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Set up crews and cost codes in timekeeping
steps.description: The general foreman adds new hires and moved workers to the right crew and project in the timekeeping app and checks the cost codes for the planned pours exist, so foremen can enter hours.

error.defect_description: Worker set up on the wrong project.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Visit sites to walk upcoming work
steps.description: The general foreman drives to the projects with large pours coming up, walks the work with the superintendent and foreman and confirms forms, access and crane time are ready.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Re-plan daily for weather and pour readiness
steps.description: Through the week the general foreman checks forecasts and calls from superintendents each evening, and decides whether rain, cold, a failed inspection or a late rebar crew means a crew must move to another project.

evidence.note: Share of weeks with at least one crew move is an estimate.

steps.name: Reshuffle crews and notify
steps.description: The general foreman moves crews between projects, calls the foremen and superintendents affected and updates the crew board so timekeeping and the next week's plan reflect the change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Reconcile planned against actual crew hours
steps.description: After the week the general foreman compares the crew board with timekeeping hours by project and notes idle crews, overtime and pours that slipped, which feeds next week's plan and the cost report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

exceptions.name: Union hall cannot fill the request
exceptions.description: In the busy season the hall sends fewer trades than requested or sends them late; the director borrows a crew from another region or the project moves a pour.

exceptions.name: Mid-week reshuffle
exceptions.description: Rain, cold, a failed pre-pour inspection or a late rebar crew forces crews to move mid-week.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from labour requests to week reconciled
benchmarks.population: Weekly regional crew plans in a Canadian union general contractor

evidence.note: Requests arrive mid-week, the plan is set at a Thursday or Friday call, the week runs Monday to Friday or Saturday and is reconciled the next Monday or Tuesday.

pain_points.description: The crew board lives in a spreadsheet and phone calls; changes during the week are not always passed to timekeeping or to the superintendents, so crews arrive at the wrong site or wait.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Pours compete for the same experienced foremen and formwork sets, and projects push their own dates at the weekly call.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Superintendents over-request crews to protect their schedule, so the general foreman has to second-guess every request against the lookahead.

evidence.note: Estimate.

assumptions: Touch times on the first step are the total across all superintendents feeding one regional plan.
The workflow follows one plan from requests to the reconciliation after the week; the week itself is waiting time before reconciliation.
Operations managers and the yard coordinator take part although the org file's process map lists only the director, general foremen and superintendents.
No crew resource is tied up by planning; crews are allocated, not occupied, so only the general foreman's pickup truck is listed.
No surge is given: the plan is weekly all year; the seasonal swing shows in the hire and layoff branches.
No web source was found that describes crew planning at a Canadian contractor; every figure is a tier C estimate.
